rule: This register is the stratum's own answer to docs/NON_CLAIMS.md: it records, per surface, whether it is `claimed` (a passing court covers it) or `bounded` (explicitly outside this stratum -- including version universality, only the exercised delta claimed, unknown staying unknown, the two planes RT-ATLAS-DELTA recorded `not-measured`, and the prohibition on reintroducing a 3.6.3 behaviour that corresponds to an upstream security fix). It is authored, not derived: the `MAINTENANCE-BOUNDARY-REGISTER` court in forensics/tools/phase21_courts.py re-reads the four passing delta courts' own records (the claimed side) and the constitution/limitations artefacts docs/RELEASE_GATES.md section 8, docs/NON_CLAIMS.md, docs/PARITY_MODEL.md section 1 and docs/SECURITY_DIVERGENCE_POLICY.md plus the two `not-measured` planes (the bounded side), and fails the stratum if any recorded boundary has drifted from the evidence that establishes it (docs/PHASE-21-SUBPHASES.md section 3.6). A surface no passing court reaches is `bounded`, never `claimed`, and every bounded row names what would make its surface measurable, so it is a stated distance rather than motionless. Nothing here is a version-universality claim: a passing delta court measures the movement between the two named authorities and nothing beyond them.

evidence.direction: added means present in 'to', absent in 'from'

surfaces.note: claimed as an instrument: the passing court admitted the delta input pair and recorded each authority's identity and build profile from forensics/authorities/AUTHORITIES.json, the two SOURCE_MANIFEST.{3.6.3,3.6.4}.json source identities, the build records and the differential that names the pair. It records the pair's identity, not the delta between them, and it fixes the direction docs/SECURITY_DIVERGENCE_POLICY.md section 1 makes security-load-bearing (historical -> production, never the reverse).
surfaces.surface: the delta input pair's admission and identity -- `openssl-3.6.3-historical` versus `openssl-3.6.4-production` -- and the fixed trajectory direction
surfaces.would_make_measurable: a different (or newly admitted) authority pair named as the delta's input, with its own source manifest, build record and differential committed before any movement is computed

surfaces.note: claimed as an instrument, and bounded to the planes it measured: the passing court recomputed the added / removed / changed delta across the atlas planes docs/PHASE-21-SUBPHASES.md section 2 names and required the committed differential to agree. Only the exports plane is measured (its two sides are committed); the provider registration-row and prerequisite-unit planes are `not-measured` and are carried as the two bounded rows below, never counted motionless.
surfaces.surface: the added / removed / changed movement across the exports plane -- the per-authority symbol and declared-surface atlases, keyed exactly as forensics/tools/atlas_differential.py keys them
surfaces.would_make_measurable: a plane whose two authority sides are both committed and compared by a differential tool, which is what makes the exports plane measured and the two named planes not

surfaces.note: claimed as an instrument, not as 'the delta is implemented': the passing court dispositioned every delta row against the candidate's own installed surface (artifacts/phase2/install/include/openssl/), a measured row `implemented` only when that surface carries the declaration with the authority's value, a `not-measured` plane or axis `boundary`, and zero unexplained. It carries zero findings on the current tree; a real un-dispositioned row would be a finding and a `fail`, and an un-dispositioned row is `UNKNOWN`, never a resting state.
surfaces.surface: the disposition of every delta row -- `implemented` / `deferred` / `not-in-profile` / `boundary` -- with zero unexplained
surfaces.would_make_measurable: every delta row the atlas-delta court computes being carried by the candidate's surface, so no row is left un-dispositioned

surfaces.note: claimed as an instrument: the passing court derived, mechanically from the dispositioned delta and the coverage atlas's export -> court edge, which courts each moving row reaches, and re-derived exactly those 20 courts over the two strata the two added macros own. The probes were NOT re-executed (mode `re-derived`, `reexecuted_courts` 0), so it records which courts the re-run step would run rather than implying a re-run that did not happen.
surfaces.surface: the derivation of which courts a delta touches, recorded with the selection derivation, so the delta reaches exactly the courts its obligations do
surfaces.would_make_measurable: a delta row whose declaring header owns a stratum whose registry stages courts, so the row reaches a court the selection can re-derive

surfaces.note: bounded: docs/RELEASE_GATES.md section 8 makes OpenSSL 4.x a major-family transition that gets a new compatibility profile, and an OpenSSL 3 receipt is never silently reinterpreted as evidence for OpenSSL 4; docs/NON_CLAIMS.md section 3 states the same as 'No version universality. An OpenSSL 3.6.x receipt is not evidence for OpenSSL 4.x.' This stratum's two authorities are both 3.6.x, so the trajectory it measures is a maintenance delta within one compatibility profile and cannot be widened by a passing court.
surfaces.surface: OpenSSL 4.x as a new compatibility profile -- a 3.x receipt reinterpreted as evidence for 4
surfaces.would_make_measurable: a newly admitted OpenSSL 4.x authority with its own source identity, atlas and oracle differential, and the court families measured under the 4.x profile -- never a 3.x receipt reused

surfaces.note: bounded: docs/PHASE-21-SUBPHASES.md section 0 and section 4.3 name 'only the exercised delta is claimed' as a load-bearing non-claim -- the delta this stratum carries is exactly the movement between the two authorities it names (the 3.6.3 -> 3.6.4 trajectory) and no more. The absence of movement elsewhere is not measured, so no court may generalise it.
surfaces.surface: only the exercised delta is claimed -- the movement between the two named authorities, not the absence of movement elsewhere
surfaces.would_make_measurable: the same delta procedure run over another named authority pair, with its own committed differential, so a second trajectory is measured rather than assumed

surfaces.note: bounded: docs/PARITY_MODEL.md section 1 makes `UNKNOWN` distinct from `FAIL` and says unknown is a research result, never traded for confidence theatre; docs/NON_CLAIMS.md section 4 states it and requires it reported precisely, not hidden. An un-dispositioned delta row is `UNKNOWN`, so unknown staying unknown bounds every other delta claim -- a passing court does not resolve it.
surfaces.surface: unknown stays unknown -- an un-dispositioned delta row is `UNKNOWN`, a research result, never a resting state
surfaces.would_make_measurable: an investigation that dispositions the row against the candidate's surface, which is what makes a delta row measured rather than unknown

surfaces.note: bounded: docs/SECURITY_DIVERGENCE_POLICY.md section 3 prohibits reintroducing a security regression to match a historical authority, and section 1 fixes the trajectory from `openssl-3.6.3-historical` to `openssl-3.6.4-production` (the security-fix release). The delta runs historical -> production and follows the fixed authority, so a 3.6.3 behaviour that corresponds to an upstream security fix is not reintroduced; the disposition court's `removed`/`changed` axis is where that prohibition is enforced.
surfaces.surface: a 3.6.3 behaviour corresponding to an upstream security fix is not reintroduced
surfaces.would_make_measurable: the fixed authority itself moving away from the fix, so no security divergence remains to be prohibited

surfaces.note: bounded, not motionless: RT-ATLAS-DELTA recorded the provider registration-row plane `not-measured` because the named census forensics/atlas/provider-algorithms.json is generated for the production authority only, no committed historical counterpart exists (forensics/atlas/openssl-3.6.3-historical carries only provider-inventory.json), and atlas_differential.py does not compare that census. The differential's adjacent provider-inventory measurement is a different artefact and is never counted as this named plane. What would make it measurable is a second provider-algorithms.json census generated over the historical authority's provider tables, exactly as the court's reason records.
surfaces.surface: the provider registration-row plane RT-ATLAS-DELTA recorded `not-measured` -- bounded, not counted motionless
surfaces.would_make_measurable: a second provider-algorithms.json census generated over the historical authority's provider tables, so the two authorities' registration rows can be set-diffed

surfaces.note: bounded, not motionless: RT-ATLAS-DELTA recorded the prerequisite-unit plane `not-measured` because forensics/prerequisites.json is a single-authority openssl-rs artefact (the implementation's prerequisite/divergence units, not an authority's), with no committed historical counterpart and no differential tool that compares it. What would make it measurable is a committed historical counterpart to that plane and a differential tool that compares the two, exactly as the court's reason records.
surfaces.surface: the prerequisite-unit plane RT-ATLAS-DELTA recorded `not-measured` -- bounded, not counted motionless
surfaces.would_make_measurable: a committed historical counterpart to forensics/prerequisites.json (the authority's own prerequisite/divergence units) and a differential tool that compares it, so the authority-to-authority unit delta can be computed
